title: Introduction to the C Programming Language
learningObjectives: Define C as a general-purpose, compiled, procedural programming language and describe the kinds of systems in which it is used.
Explain why C remains important for operating systems, embedded software, compilers, libraries and performance-sensitive applications.
Distinguish C source code from the compiler, linker, executable program and runtime environment.
Read a minimal hosted C program and identify its header inclusion, main function, output call and return status.
Describe the difference between learning C syntax and writing reliable, portable C programs.

understand.concept: C is a general-purpose programming language designed to express programs with close control over data, memory and execution. It is commonly used in operating-system components, embedded devices, device drivers, compilers, interpreters, databases, networking software and performance-sensitive libraries. C gives programmers powerful tools—such as functions, arrays, structures and pointers—but also requires them to reason carefully about object lifetime, bounds, types and resource ownership. C source code is not executed directly by an ordinary web browser: it is translated by a C implementation toolchain for a target environment.
understand.whyItMatters: C is both a practical language and a way to understand how software interacts with computers. Learning it builds a strong foundation in data representation, memory, compilation, debugging and program design. These ideas are useful when studying other languages, operating systems, security, embedded development and performance engineering.
understand.analogy: A C source file is like a set of detailed construction plans. A compiler toolchain checks and translates those plans for a target platform; the resulting executable is the built product.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only an introduction. A compiler does not guarantee that a program is logically correct or safe. C programs must still obey language rules, use valid memory, handle errors and be tested on their intended targets.

explain.narrative:
C is a standardized language with a long history in systems programming. Its design makes many machine-level details visible to the programmer while still providing portable language constructs and a standard library. That balance explains why C appears in software that needs predictable resource use, access to low-level interfaces or compatibility with established system APIs. C is not automatically faster or better than every other language; the right choice depends on the product, safety requirements, team skills and available libraries.

A C program is normally written in one or more source files, commonly ending in .c. Header files provide declarations and are included with preprocessing directives such as #include. A compiler translates each source file according to a selected C language version and target. A linker combines the resulting object files with required libraries. The operating system or target runtime then loads and executes the program. The exact commands and stages vary by toolchain, but separating these responsibilities makes build errors easier to diagnose.

The following small program is a hosted C example. The standard header stdio.h declares the puts function. The function main is the entry point for a hosted program. The call to puts writes a line to the standard output stream, and returning zero reports successful termination to the host environment. This is a starting point, not the whole language: later lessons will explain statements, expressions, types, input, control flow, functions, arrays, pointers and memory.

C is case-sensitive, has a defined grammar and has several standardized language versions. A program that compiles with one compiler extension may not be portable to another implementation. Learn to compile with warnings enabled, read diagnostics, test boundary cases and consult the language and library documentation instead of relying on accidental behaviour.

examples.title: Your first hosted C program
examples.explanation: The preprocessing directive makes the declaration of puts available. main is the hosted-program entry point. puts writes the text followed by a newline. Returning 0 indicates successful termination.

examples.title: A function that computes a value
examples.explanation: This example introduces a separate function, an int parameter, a return value, a local variable and formatted output. The next lessons will explain each construct in detail.

practise.guidedTask: In a C compiler environment, create a source file named main.c. Type the first example, compile it, run it and record the exact compiler command and output. Then explain—in your own words—what the header, main function, puts call and return statement each do.
practise.independentTask: Write a short C program that prints three lines: your name, one problem you would like software to solve, and one reason you are learning C. Compile with warnings enabled. Change one line, rebuild and run again. Keep both the source file and the command you used.
hints: Use a C compiler such as GCC, Clang or a supported vendor toolchain; an editor alone does not compile C.
For a hosted program, use int main(void) when the program takes no command-line arguments.
Include <stdio.h> when using standard I/O functions such as puts or printf.
A successful compilation does not prove the program is correct; read warnings and test the result.
Do not assume undefined behaviour has a predictable result.

questions.prompt: Which description best characterizes the C programming language?
options: A general-purpose language commonly used for systems and application software
A markup language used to describe web page structure
A stylesheet language used only for page colours
questions.answer: A general-purpose language commonly used for systems and application software
questions.explanation: C is a general-purpose programming language used in systems software, embedded development and many other domains.

questions.prompt: Why is C commonly used in systems and embedded development?
options: It provides control over data representation, memory and execution
It removes the need to understand memory or hardware interfaces
It runs as plain text in every web browser
questions.answer: It provides control over data representation, memory and execution
questions.explanation: C exposes low-level mechanisms while retaining standardized language constructs.

questions.prompt: What normally translates C source code into object code or an executable?
questions.explanation: The compiler and associated build tools translate source code and link required objects and libraries.

questions.prompt: In a hosted C program, what is the usual role of main?
options: It is the program entry point
It declares every function in the standard library
questions.answer: It is the program entry point
questions.explanation: A hosted C program begins execution through main, using one of the forms defined by the C standard.

questions.prompt: What does returning 0 from main conventionally communicate to the host environment?
options: That the program has no variables
questions.explanation: Zero is the conventional success status returned by a hosted program.
